newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse lists its 48th stock.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse lists its 48th stock.

text.p: Morocco on Wednesday listed silver mine Imiter on the Casablanca stock exchange -- the 12th stock listed since the government launched a privatisation programme in 1993, bringing the total number of companies listed on the emerging bourse to 48.
"Silver mine firm Imiter, which was floated on the market from 9 to 13 June, was listed on Wednesday on the bourse as the 48th stock," a bourse spokeswoman said.
The bourse also has 30 mutual funds and 12 brokerage houses.
Reuters Identification Code (RIC) was not yet available.

"The firm shares were demanded at 407.85 dirhams but there were no Imiter shares for sale," a broker at Upline Securities said. "The market is adopting a wait and see position over the silver mine trend."
The privatisation ministry recently sold a 20 percent stake in Imiter worth 130.3 million dirhams ($13.7 million), or 396 dirhams per share.

The bourse had a total market capitalisation of 111 billion dirhams ($11.6 billion) in the first quarter of the year, or nearly double the amount in the previous period, a market analyst at Casbalnca Finance Intermediation (CFI) said.
According to CFI, foreign investment, which represents an estimated five to six percent of total market capitalisation has remained unchanged since 1995.
